summary: My slot was the batch/step-count budget. I bracketed it: 2**19=1.0123, 2**18=1.0037 (a0), 2**17=1.0096, and showed sqrt-style LR downscaling at small batch hurts (1.0117 vs 1.0096) and that raising Muon LR 0.04->0.06 hurts (1.0046 vs 1.0013), so batch 2**18 with the stock LRs is the right operating point and LR magnitude is bracketed on both sides. Three ideas of mine failed and are on the record: a speedrun-style batch-size ramp (grad_accum 1->2->4, 1.0083 vs 1.0037), value embeddings on every layer instead of alternating (0.9958; +44M params cost 20% of the tokens), and the big four-way capacity stack, which never beat plain depth12. My last run was spoiled by running arena-adopt after editing train.py, so it was an exact replicate of a1's b48980c -- which at least gives the cell its only noise estimate: 0.986500 vs 0.986243, i.e. ~0.0003 run-to-run at fixed seed, so sub-0.001 gaps in this cell are noise. Next I would test the untested cheap composition (depth12 + short window 512 + per-channel lambdas), then re-check batch size at the final architecture, since per-step cost has roughly doubled since 2**18 was chosen.
